proposal.title: Industrial PhD Proposal: Mitigation of Biomass Fouling in Spiral-Wound Ultrafiltration Membranes for Bioprocess Streams
proposal.summary: This three-year industrial PhD project tackles severe membrane fouling during fermentation broth ultrafiltration at Ferment-Pro d.o.o. by combining advanced fouling characterisation with optimised pre-treatment and cleaning-in-place protocols. Led by an experienced doctoral candidate under the supervision of Professor Ivona Bogdanović, the research bridges laboratory-scale membrane science with authentic industrial processing conditions. The collaboration targets a reduction in cleaning frequency, restoring nominal throughput and eliminating the 11% production cost penalty.
proposal.problem: Ferment-Pro d.o.o. suffers from severe membrane fouling during downstream ultrafiltration of fermentation broths, causing operations to run at only 55% of nominal throughput [C144-CH2]. Membranes foul within 36 hours instead of the targeted 72 hours, forcing two cleaning cycles per batch and adding 11% to total production costs [C144-CH2]. Whole cells and cell debris passing through the existing depth-filter setup contribute to this rapid fouling of the 10 kDa spiral-wound polyethersulfone membranes [C144-CH2].
researchQuestions: How do residual whole cells and cell debris breaking through depth filters interact with 10 kDa spiral-wound polyethersulfone membranes to govern flux decline and irreversible fouling resistance?
To what extent can targeted enzymatic pre-treatment or modified pre-filtration mitigate biomass deposition on 10 kDa polyethersulfone membranes during fermentation broth ultrafiltration?
What cleaning-in-place protocol adjustments can reliably restore pure water flux and extend membrane operational life from 36 hours to the target 72 hours per cycle?

plan.work: Characterise authentic industrial feed streams and fouled 10 kDa spiral-wound polyethersulfone membranes using resistance-in-series models and foulant analysis in the university laboratory.
plan.result: Quantification of reversible and irreversible fouling resistances and identification of exact foulant composition from Ferment-Pro production batches.

plan.work: Evaluate pre-treatment strategies, including protease pre-treatment adaptations and pre-filtration enhancements, on bench-scale cross-flow ultrafiltration rigs using authentic fermentation broths.
plan.result: Validated pre-treatment protocol that increases limiting flux and prevents premature biomass accumulation on the membrane surface.

plan.work: Implement and validate optimized cleaning-in-place protocols and integrated pre-treatment on industrial pilot and production lines at Ferment-Pro d.o.o.
plan.result: Extended operational cycle duration from 36 hours to 72 hours, elimination of extra cleaning cycles, and verified reduction of total production costs.

proposal.title: Motion-Aware Filtering to Reduce False Atrial Fibrillation Alarms in Patch ECG Devices
proposal.summary: CardioTrack d.o.o. faces a significant clinical bottleneck where roughly one in four atrial fibrillation alerts in their clinician portal turn out to be motion artifacts. To solve this, Associate Professor Maja Popović will supervise a three-year industrial PhD candidate to integrate her motion-aware filtering framework into CardioTrack's resource-constrained wearable patch. The collaboration leverages CardioTrack's existing three-axis accelerometer data logging at 50 Hz and the researcher's published expertise in false alarm reduction.
proposal.problem: CardioTrack d.o.o. deals with too many false atrial fibrillation alarms when patients move. When a patient walks fast, reaches overhead, or rolls over in bed, electrode contact changes momentarily and the raw signal looks enough like atrial fibrillation that the current classifier flags it. Right now, roughly one in four AF alerts that land in the clinician portal turns out to be a motion artifact once the cardiologist looks at the raw trace. Clinicians are starting to ignore low-confidence flags entirely, which defeats the purpose of automatic detection.
researchQuestions: How can single-lead ECG signals and 50 Hz three-axis accelerometer data be fused on resource-constrained microcontrollers to suppress motion artifacts without introducing processing latency?
What adaptive threshold mechanisms can minimize false-positive atrial fibrillation rates during high-motion intervals across diverse patient populations?

plan.work: Adapt and optimize the motion-aware filtering algorithm for offline processing using CardioTrack's existing patient recordings and benchmark datasets.
plan.result: A validated signal processing pipeline implemented in Python that achieves a target reduction in false atrial fibrillation alerts on historical recordings.

plan.work: Port the optimized filtering algorithms to embedded C for the Nordic nRF5340 SoC and integrate with TensorFlow Lite for on-device inference.
plan.result: An embedded firmware prototype running on the physical patch hardware that processes simultaneous ECG and 50 Hz accelerometer streams in real time.

plan.work: Conduct bench testing, validate performance against IEC 62304 standards, and complete the doctoral dissertation.
plan.result: A fully tested firmware module ready for regulatory integration and a successfully defended industrial PhD thesis.

proposal.title: Industrial PhD Proposal: Day-Ahead Feeder-Level PV Forecasting Models for Distribution Networks
proposal.summary: GridSense Analytics and Dr. Tamara Simić will develop, containerize, and deploy day-ahead PV forecasting models for distribution network feeders to resolve inaccurate load profiles caused by rooftop solar penetration. The three-year industrial PhD will translate advanced satellite cloud data methodologies into a production-grade Azure environment. Both parties will jointly bridge the gap between academic forecasting models and scalable energy software architecture.
proposal.problem: Rooftop solar installations are growing rapidly in the areas GridSense Analytics customers serve, meaning standard load profiles no longer reflect actual feeder flows at midday on sunny days. Some feeders now show reverse power flow in the afternoon, causing switching and maintenance decisions to be off by thirty percent or more. Although the company possesses half-hourly smart meter reads, airport weather station data, and licensed satellite irradiance estimates, they lack a model that produces a per-feeder load forecast twenty-four hours ahead, updated each evening and capable of running on a small Azure virtual machine within their existing FastAPI and Docker stack.
researchQuestions: How can hybrid convolutional-recurrent neural network architectures processing satellite cloud motion imagery and numerical weather data be optimized to run within the computational limits of a small Azure virtual machine?
To what extent can day-ahead per-feeder load forecasting errors driven by reverse power flow from rooftop PV be reduced compared to baseline standard load profiles?
What model compression and feature reduction techniques maintain day-ahead forecast accuracy while meeting the operational evening update schedule of GridSense Analytics?

plan.work: Data ingestion pipeline development and baseline model adaptation using historical smart meter reads, airport weather data, and satellite irradiance estimates.
plan.result: A validated core forecasting prototype running in a local Python environment that predicts per-feeder loads twenty-four hours ahead.

plan.work: Model containerization, optimization, and integration into the GridSense Analytics FastAPI and Docker stack for deployment on a small Azure virtual machine.
plan.result: A lightweight, containerized machine learning service that executes the evening update schedule without exceeding Azure compute budgets.

plan.work: Field testing on live distribution feeder datasets, performance benchmarking against operator requirements, and thesis finalization.
plan.result: A fully evaluated production-ready forecasting module, an industrial PhD dissertation, and co-authored technical publications.

proposal.summary: This one-year joint project integrates deterministic clinical rules into Kognitiva's Python and Spark stack to detect nuanced medical coding inconsistencies. By combining Kognitiva's bulk commercial insurance dataset with Róbert Fehér's clinical informatics expertise, the project addresses the 3.2 percent error rate causing significant reimbursement losses. proposal.problem: Kognitiva a.d. processes bulk health-insurance claims where approximately 3.2 percent of records contain mismatched diagnosis and procedure codes. researchQuestions: How can deterministic clinical rules from past academic work be mapped directly into Kognitiva's existing Python and Spark stack to flag diagnostic and therapeutic inconsistencies in bulk insurance claims?
